messages:
alice (runtime): heads up — noticed a weird tail-latency shape on streaming responses after the last kernel selector change. p99 jumps ~2.8x for some customers when chunk_size=64 tokens. smaller chunks look better for perceived latency, but throughput drops. anyone else seeing this?
ben (infra): can you paste the perf numbers and config? sounds like microbatching + kernel choice might be interacting. :thinking: 
alice (runtime): repro config: `model=v1.3-q4`, `stream_chunk_tokens=64`, `flush_interval_ms=50`, microbatch target=32. steady qps = 120 req/s. observed: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=560ms. switching `stream_chunk_tokens=8` -> p50=40ms, p95=90ms, p99=220ms, but overall tokens/sec drops ~18%.
carol (perf): thanks — that p99 delta screams tail scheduling + KV-cache churn. small flushes create lots of tiny KV cache lookups/updates and can force more context switches. did you profile per-stage (encode, kv, attention, postproc)?
dmitri (mlopt): kernel selector note: for that model and these seq lengths, we pick the fused-attn kernel for seq>=32 which is high-throughput, but it has longer per-batch setup and is sensitive to uneven microbatch fill. with small streaming chunks we end up with many underfilled microbatches which trigger slower fallback kernels or poor warp utilization.
eva (sre): also check RPC batching at the ingress layer — lots of tiny streaming frames can blow up scheduling in the request router. we saw similar with short flush intervals in staging last month.
alice (runtime): below is a tiny snippet of the rollout config I'm testing:
```
streaming:
  stream_chunk_tokens: 64  # try 8/16/32
  flush_interval_ms: 50
microbatching:
  target_microbatch: 32
  max_batch_delay_ms: 30
```
carol (perf): can you run a per-kernel flame for the two configs? i want time spent in `kv_lookup` vs `attn_fused` vs `matmul` and also counts of `kv_merge` ops. small chunks -> kv_merge count explodes.
alice (runtime): ran a quick flame. results (median of 10 runs):
- chunk=64: attn_fused 48%, matmul 12%, kv_lookup 10%, kv_merge 3%, overhead 27%
- chunk=8: attn_fused 22%, matmul 9%, kv_lookup 28%, kv_merge 18%, overhead 23%
so kv_lookup+kv_merge go way up for small chunks.
dmitri (mlopt): that matches theory: small streaming fragments blow up KV access ops relative to compute. also fused kernels are starved by many small microbatches so effective throughput per-GPU falls. for p99, contention + scheduling jitter explains the tail.
ben (infra): two levers: 1) increase `max_batch_delay_ms` to allow microbatches to fill (improve kernel efficiency), or 2) change streaming flush heuristic to coalesce multiple small chunks into a single flush at the routing layer (emit smaller perceived chunks to client but only commit to worker when aggregate reaches threshold).
eva (sre): be careful: adding delay increases real latency for the first tokens. perceived latency for streaming is about when first chunk hits client. we need to balance first-byte delay vs tail token throughput. product asked for sub-100ms first-byte p95.
carol (perf): propose a hybrid heuristic: immediate flush for first chunk (to satisfy perceived latency), then buffer subsequent chunks up to N tokens or T ms before dispatching to workers. that reduces KV churn while keeping first-byte low.
alice (runtime): sounds good. i sketched a patch: if client_first_chunk=true -> flush immediately, then start coalescing. pseudo:
```
if is_first_chunk: send_immediately()
else:
  buffer += chunk
  if buffer.tokens >= COALESCE_TOKENS or buffer.ms >= COALESCE_MS:
    flush(buffer)
```
we can tune COALESCE_TOKENS per-model (e.g., depend on avg seq length) and prefer kernels that like mid-sized batches.
dmitri (mlopt): +1. also add a metric `kv_merge_per_req` and `microbatch_fill_ratio`. we can then auto-tune COALESCE_TOKENS to hit target fill ratio (e.g., >= 0.7) while keeping first-byte delay < X ms.
eva (sre): how about rollout plan? we should run canary at 5% traffic with detailed histograms for p50/p95/p99 and a broken-down KV op count.
nice (deploy-bot): deploy scheduled: runtime/stream-coalesce v2 -> canary 5% at 1752016000 by dmitri. :rocket: 
carol (perf): quick target numbers to aim for in canary vs baseline:
- first-byte p95 <= 100ms (must meet product)
- throughput within -10% of baseline tokens/sec
- p99 improved or unchanged
if coalescing hits these, we can expand to 25%.
ben (infra): one more caveat: kernel selector needs to be aware of expected microbatch fill. if coalescer guarantees fills >= X we can force fused kernel path earlier. add a hint in the request envelope: `expected_fill_ratio` to help runtime choose kernel.
dmitri (mlopt): i'll add the hint and an override in the selector for canary. will also add the auto-tune job that sweeps COALESCE_TOKENS in staging.
alice (runtime): i'll run the canary harness with the two model variants and post the full traces. thanks all. :thumbsup: 
carol (perf): also capture tail-latency pdfs (not just p95/p99). shape matters. if you can attach ridgeline plots that helps the PM decide tradeoffs.
eva (sre): and add alert rule: if p99 for streaming increases >1.5x vs baseline for 5m, rollback.
alice (runtime): noted. filing follow-ups: perf-traces link: https://internal.perf/1752008765-traces (will populate after runs).
